I'll read both files now.Let me read the rest of the findings file.I have now read the entire section and the complete findings file (all 1199 lines). Let me verify my assessment of the key quantitative claims and citation attributions.

After a thorough check of every concrete claim in the section against the tagged findings:

- All numerical results (Nash–Sutcliffe/EF values, drain spacings, percentages, seepage fractions, confidence-interval widths, RRMSE/NSE/KGE values, salt-discharge increases, drawdown values, etc.) trace correctly to their cited papers (e.g., Gowda2012 EF values, Wang2006 CI widths, Xin2016b order-of-magnitude over-prediction, Askar2020 macropore results, Karan2021 13%/31%, AbdElaty2019 12.5–43.4%, Han2025 16.9–55.7×, DarziNaftchally2014 30 m vs 55 m, AbdelFattah2005 23–74%, Kirkham1997 160–270%).
- Each concrete claim's primary source is correctly attributed. Grouped multi-citations (e.g., SIDRA family, MODFLOW regional, dual-permeability) each contain the correct supporting key(s).
- General framing/overview sentences are domain-appropriate and not overstated beyond the evidence.

A few grouped citations append topically-adjacent same-author/same-topic works (e.g., Awad2022b beside the correct Awad2022 for DRAINMOD-ANN; Saadat2018/Österholm2015 beside Youssef2021 for controlled drainage), but in every case the correct primary paper is cited and no claim is attributed solely to a wrong/swapped key, and no number is invented or unsupported.
